new.title: Agent guesses the reconciliation tickets.db location and schema by trial and error
new.cause: No discoverable pointer gives the path and schema of the reconciliation tickets store. The agent probed several candidate paths (fused-memory/data/tickets.db, data/reconciliation/tickets.db, data/queue/tickets.db). It hit 'no such table: tickets' on one file and 'no such column: id' on another, which costs several turns per forensic read. CLAUDE.md offers scripts/tasks_db_schema.py only for the tasks store.

verdict.severity_reason: This costs a few wasted turns per forensic read of the tickets store. It does not affect correctness or any change to the code.
verdict.reason: The tree still has no pointer to the reconciliation tickets store's path or schema. The only schema-introspection script in scripts/ is tasks_db_schema.py, which covers the tasks store. CLAUDE.md's 'Forensic reads of tasks.db' section covers only the tasks store and never mentions tickets.db. The only operator-facing mention of the tickets store is a single sqlite3 example in OPERATIONS.md at line 812, which uses the relative path data/reconciliation/tickets.db and lists no columns. The path is otherwise defined only in source files such as main_checkout_defaults.py and tools.py, where an agent doing a forensic read would not look.
verdict.proposal: Extend the 'Forensic reads of tasks.db' section to name the reconciliation tickets store's canonical path and say how to get its schema, for example by pointing at scripts/tasks_db_schema.py with --db if it accepts that store, or at a small schema-dump script.

new.title: Digest not_found at turns exceeding session turn count
new.cause: Digest extraction is indexing into turn numbers (67, 148) that do not exist in a 1-user-turn session, suggesting either session-boundary confusion, turn-number misattribution from a prior/different session, or off-by-one indexing in turn reconstruction

verdict.severity_reason: The label misleads a reader of the digest and makes miners flag false anomalies. The data is correct and nothing operational breaks.
verdict.reason: Confirmed in the current tree. scripts/legibility/digest.py renders each digest item as "(turn {item['index']})" (for example _render_user_corrections, line 773). That `index` comes from enumerate() over ALL transcript records: _signal_items enumerates the per-record hits, and _error_neighborhoods enumerates the per-record errors. Records include assistant messages and tool_results. n_user_turns is a separate count, len(iter_user_turns(records)), which includes only user turns. So "turn 67" or "turn 148" is a record position, not a user-turn number, and it can be far above n_user_turns, or appear when n_user_turns is 0. The "turn" label is a name that says one thing while the value is another. The "does not exist" text is a not_found hit literal that a tool_result contained. It is not the digest reporting a missing turn. I did not check whether other digest renderers use the same label. The reported phantom turn numbers are explained by this label and need no session-boundary confusion or off-by-one indexing.
verdict.proposal: Change the rendered '(turn N)' labels to '(record N)', or an equivalent name that says N is a transcript record index, so they cannot be confused with the n_user_turns count.

new.title: Interactive agent session with zero user turns contradicts session class
new.cause: Session classified as 'interactive' but n_user_turns: 0 indicates no user engagement occurred; combined with early termination (size_bytes: 412) and single incomplete guard signal, suggests bootstrap/initialization failure or session-classification misattribution

verdict.severity_reason: The mislabel only skews digest and census triage metadata. It does not affect operation, and score_signals already weights n_user_turns separately.
verdict.reason: The pairing is still produced by the current code. In scripts/legibility/detectors.py, `AgentClassEvidence.agent_class` returns `AgentClass.INTERACTIVE` whenever the session has records, is not in a worktree dir, and matches no marker. Its docstring says 'No marker is INTERACTIVE', so interactive is the residual default, not a positive finding. It does not look at user turns. A session with no primary user turn therefore still gets `agent_class: interactive`, and `n_user_turns` is computed separately in digest.py, so a digest can carry `agent_class: interactive` with `n_user_turns: 0`. I did not check the individual sessions. Worktree-run sessions are labelled orchestrated-task only when the encoded dir contains a `WORKTREE_DIR_MARKERS` substring. A session in a worktree path that matches none of them also falls back to interactive. The 'bootstrap failure' reading in the cluster is a guess I could not verify; the verifiable fact is that the class name overstates what the classifier knows.
verdict.proposal: In AgentClassEvidence.agent_class, return AgentClass.UNKNOWN (or a new distinct class) instead of INTERACTIVE when no primary user turn was observed, so INTERACTIVE only labels sessions with a real user turn.

new.title: Digest 'User Corrections' bucket mislabels injected task context/briefing as a correction
new.cause: Digest pipeline confuses task-instruction boilerplate (adjudication rubric, prior-round reference list, context) with actual user-provided feedback corrections

verdict.severity_reason: Fabricated gold 'User Corrections' mislead digest consumers and inflate n_user_turns scoring. The effect is contained to one injector shape in the digest pipeline.
verdict.reason: The gold-turn filter `scripts/legibility/digest.py::iter_user_turns` drops injected turns through `reingestion.is_harness_injected_turn`. That predicate matches only briefing headings, heading sets, the prose markers in `HARNESS_PROMPT_MARKERS`, and memory-context caveat markers. The prior-round adjudication prompt is built in `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/review_suggestions/prior_round.py` and opens 'You are adjudicating whether each CURRENT review suggestion merely re-flags...'. No marker in `scripts/legibility/` covers that text, so it still passes as a human turn and renders under '## User Corrections'. Other shapes in the cluster, such as '# Context' and the briefing, are probably already filtered by the existing rules (instrument versions 2-6). I did not check the '(turn 3) The implementation was reviewed and blocking issues were found' wording or the '/prd decompose' command-args turn. The adjudication-prompt shape is confirmed still unguarded.
verdict.proposal: Add the prior-round adjudication prompt opener ('you are adjudicating whether each current review suggestion merely re-flags') to HARNESS_PROMPT_MARKERS, and bump DIGEST_INSTRUMENT_VERSION in scripts/legibility/digest.py.

new.title: Digest 'User Corrections' bucket captures skill invocations and task notifications
new.cause: Digest extraction treats /unblock skill command and task-completion notifications as user corrections when they are neither corrections nor user-originated feedback.

verdict.severity_reason: Contained noise in a diagnostic digest. The main harm, injected and notification turns, is already filtered, and the remaining turns are few and short.
verdict.reason: Only part of the cluster still holds. The task-notification part is already fixed: scripts/legibility/digest.py::iter_user_turns now calls detectors.is_non_dialogue_carrier, and reingestion.has_non_human_origin drops records whose origin.kind is not 'human'. That filter is part of instrument version 6. The part that remains is slash-command wrapper turns (<command-name>/unblock</command-name>, <command-message>reflect</command-message>) and '[Request interrupted by user]' turns. Neither digest.py nor detectors.py::user_turn_text excludes them, and a grep of scripts/legibility finds no command-name filter in the digest path. So they still reach the 'User Corrections' section, labeled as corrections, and interrupts are also counted in the separate Interrupts bucket. These are human-typed, so the user-originated half of the claim is wrong. What remains is that the section label ('User Corrections', from digest.py's section-title table) promises more than the user_turns bucket delivers. The cost is added noise for the trickle coder.
verdict.proposal: In iter_user_turns, skip user turns whose text is only a slash-command wrapper or an '[Request interrupted by user' marker. Alternatively, rename the 'user_corrections' section label to match what it actually holds, and bump DIGEST_INSTRUMENT_VERSION.

re_observed.title: Escalation watcher emits get_task_escalations calls with an empty-valued optional parameter (`"status": ,`), producing unparseable JSON that recurs across tasks
re_observed.cause: When the watcher wants to omit the optional status filter, it writes the key with no value instead of dropping it. The harness then rejects the whole call with InputValidationError, wasting a turn. The same malformed shape recurred for tasks 6060 and 5813, 63 turns apart, so nothing carries the lesson forward. The tool's parameter docs or the watcher prompt could state that optional filters must be omitted, not left blank.

new.observation: The reconciliation tickets store has a path defined in source (main_checkout_defaults.py, tools.py) and one relative-path sqlite3 example in OPERATIONS.md, but nothing an agent doing a forensic read would reach first points at it. That is a heuristic 11, SPOT, gap of the derivation kind: the fact has one home, but no reader-facing pointer derives from it, so each agent re-derives it by probing candidate paths. The errors it met ('no such table: tickets', 'no such column: id') are the same shape CLAUDE.md already warns about for the tasks store and its 0-byte decoy, which is why they cost turns rather than a single refusal. Heuristic 1, informative names, applies to the error surface: a 'no such table' answer from a wrong file names neither the file the agent should have opened nor the store's real columns. The verdict's proposal to extend the existing 'Forensic reads' section is the smallest change that gives the fact a pointer in the place the tasks-store pointer already lives.

The verdict's evidence places this squarely under heuristic 1, informative names: the digest renders '(turn N)' where N is an enumerate() position over all transcript records, including assistant messages and tool_results, while n_user_turns counts only user turns. The label says one thing while the value is another, and a reader who trusts the label concludes a turn is missing or a session boundary slipped. Heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings, is the second leg: the record index and the user-turn count are different quantities that reach the reader only as the prose word 'turn', so the distinction is lost at the rendering boundary. The brief's cause (session-boundary confusion, turn misattribution, off-by-one) is not supported by the verified code path; the phantom numbers are fully explained by the mislabel, and the 'does not exist' text is a not_found literal from a tool_result, not the digest reporting a missing turn. The verdict did not check whether other renderers share the label, so the fix should be sought wherever index is rendered, not only in _render_user_corrections.

Per the verdict, AgentClassEvidence.agent_class returns INTERACTIVE as the residual when a session has records, is not in a worktree dir, and matches no marker; it never consults user turns. So 'interactive' is a default, not a positive finding, which fails heuristic 1, informative names: the class name claims a human was present when the classifier only knows that nothing else matched. Heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings, is engaged because the enum value INTERACTIVE is doing double duty as 'observed a user' and 'no marker matched', two states that a typed classification should keep apart (the verdict's UNKNOWN or a new class). The co-occurrence with n_user_turns: 0 is therefore a product of two independent computations in detectors.py and digest.py, not evidence of a bootstrap failure; that reading in the brief's cause was not verifiable. Worktree sessions whose encoded dir matches no WORKTREE_DIR_MARKERS substring fall into the same residual, so the mislabel is wider than zero-turn sessions.

The verdict confirms one shape in the cluster is still unguarded: the prior-round adjudication prompt built in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/review_suggestions/prior_round.py passes reingestion.is_harness_injected_turn because no entry in HARNESS_PROMPT_MARKERS, the briefing headings, or the memory-context caveats covers its opener. This is heuristic 11, SPOT, in its failure mode: the set of harness-injected prompt shapes is authored in the orchestrator and recognised in scripts/legibility by an independently maintained marker list, so each new prompt shape silently joins the gold turns until someone adds a marker. Heuristic 10, clear invariants, informatively, redundantly, uniformly enforced, names the cost: the invariant 'a gold user turn is human-typed' is enforced by one string-match list rather than by anything the injector itself stamps, so a miss is invisible. Heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings, is the root: origin is being inferred from prose markers rather than carried as a typed field. The verdict notes the '# Context' and briefing shapes are probably already filtered by instrument versions 2-6, and that two other wordings in the cluster were not checked, so the proposed marker addition closes the confirmed shape only.

Only part of this cluster survives in the current tree. Task-notification turns are already dropped: iter_user_turns calls detectors.is_non_dialogue_carrier and reingestion.has_non_human_origin filters records whose origin.kind is not 'human' (instrument version 6). What remains is slash-command wrapper turns (<command-name>/unblock</command-name>, <command-message>reflect</command-message>) and '[Request interrupted by user]' turns, which no filter in the digest path excludes. Those are human-typed, so the brief's 'not user-originated' framing is wrong for them; the verified defect is heuristic 1, informative names, at the section level: 'User Corrections' promises corrections and delivers every surviving user turn. Heuristic 6, well-defined purpose for each entity, is the shape of the fix: the user_turns bucket either filters to corrections or is renamed to what it holds, but not both at once. Heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings, applies to the command wrappers themselves, which arrive as markup inside the turn text and would need yet another string match to drop. Interrupts are additionally double-counted via the separate Interrupts bucket.

The stamp is unknown/unknown; the verdict pins the cause to the residual-default branch of AgentClassEvidence.agent_class in scripts/legibility/detectors.py, an implementation of the legibility classifier, and the mislabel shows up in digest and census triage metadata read during operations.

The stamp is unknown/unknown; the verdict places the surviving defect in scripts/legibility/digest.py::iter_user_turns lacking a slash-command and interrupt filter, an implementation gap, and it manifests when the rendered 'User Corrections' section is read by the trickle coder or an operator.

findings.statement: The agent supplied an invented 'line_range' argument alongside the real offset and limit parameters to Read. The tool schema rejected the call as an unexpected parameter, which cost a turn. The redundant range was most likely the agent's own guess at a range syntax. Nothing in the call path steers the agent to the real offset/limit contract before it guesses. Verifier: The failed call is real, but the cause is the agent's own invented argument and the Read tool's schema. The Read tool is built into the harness, and this tree does not contain it. The tree uses 'line_range' as an identifier in unrelated code, such as workflow.py, merge_lane/worker.py and tests. I found no file in the tree that teaches Read a 'line_range' parameter or that could guard against this. The confusion is not an observable property of the current tree's state, and no existing file produces it.

mcp__playwright__browser_evaluate rejects a filename under the session scratchpad (/tmp/claude-1000/<project>/<session>/scratchpad) because only the project root and .playwright-mcp are allowed roots. The agent used the scratchpad as its scratch area, so the call failed and a turn was wasted. Nothing tells the agent that the browser tool's allowed roots differ from the Bash scratchpad. Verifier: I can't confirm a cause in this tree. The quoted error is a Playwright MCP / Claude Code harness restriction on file-output roots, and the tree doesn't contain that tooling. I searched the *.md, *.yaml and *.json files for 'playwright-mcp' or 'scratchpad'. I saw no hits that define or teach a rule about those roots. The search output was capped at 20 files, and I opened only the codebook, where 'playwright' has no entry. The tree doesn't tell agents to use the scratchpad for browser output.

The entities-declaration check rejects a declaration whose referent appears in the content only in a non-canonical form such as 'task-173-...' or 'gate 184'. The workaround of omitting entities, which always succeeds, then gets recorded as durable guidance ('drop entities entirely'). Those memories defeat the structured-entity purpose of the feature, which is to stop entities being inferred from free text. The gate's accepted surface forms are not documented where authors write, so each author rediscovers the rejection by failure. Verifier: The claim is not borne out by the current tree. The `add_memory` docstring in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py does document the accepted surface form. It says a conflicting declaration is rejected with DeclaredReferentConflictRejected and to "fix the id, or write `task NNN` in the content". It also says absence is never rejected and that `id` is digits, never a label. `_LOCAL_MENTION_PATTERN` in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/utils/canonical_labels.py accepts `task` followed by `#`, `:`, whitespace, `-` or `/` and then digits. That means 'task-173-...' is recognised unless it is glued to a preceding word character, colon or hyphen. 'gate 184' is not a task mention, and the docstring directs authors to write `task NNN`. The remaining claim, that agents record 'drop entities' as durable guidance, concerns memory contents. I could not check that from the code, and there is one sighting.

A tool-use guard rejects a short foreground sleep chained with echo and directs the agent to Monitor with an until-loop or run_in_background. The agent used a plain sleep to wait for a merge request to finalize, and the rule is not in the agent's guidance, so it is learned by failure, costing a turn. The same session then polled merge_status x3 and get_merge_queue x5, which suggests no blocking wait primitive for merge finalization is advertised. Verifier: The guard itself is Claude Code harness tooling, which this tree does not contain. The tree already teaches the rule that the cluster says is missing. skills/merge-queue/SKILL.md has a 'Waiting between polls' section (anchor waiting-between-polls). It names the 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-07 harness blocks of a bare `sleep 60`. It prescribes a bounded `timeout ... bash -c 'while ...; do sleep 5; done'` loop that wakes early on git ancestry, and it explains why Monitor is not the right tool. It also covers 15s to 60s backoff polling with `merge_status`, and `merge_request(wait_secs=100)` is the blocking wait it advertises. The polling of `merge_status` x3 and `get_merge_queue` x5 is the documented design, not a missing primitive.
